title: 1997 AHSME Problem 1
statement: If \(a\) and \(b\) are digits for which \[ \begin{array}{r} 2a\\[-2pt] {}\times b3\\ \hline 69\\ 92\phantom0\\ \hline 989 \end{array} \] then \(a+b=\)

solutions.text: The first partial product says \(3(20+a)=69,\) so \(a=3.\) The second says \(23b=92,\) so \(b=4.\) Thus \(a+b=7,\) and the correct answer is C.
hints: Use the first partial product to determine the two-digit top factor
The second partial product is the top factor multiplied by \(b\)
